# MLB center fielders, 2026

The 40 qualified center fielders of the 2026 MLB season, with 11 hitting, running and fielding stats each, from Baseball Savant (Statcast). Made for the Week 10 "PCA on PCA" slides: principal component analysis with Pete Crow-Armstrong.

## Files

- `center-fielders.csv` has one row per player:
  - `player_id`: MLBAM player ID, as used by Baseball Savant
  - `player`: "Last, First"
  - `team`: team name
  - `pa`: plate appearances
  - `hr`: home runs (not used in the PCA; `iso` covers power)
  - `k_pct`, `bb_pct`: strikeouts and walks, as a percent of plate appearances
  - `chase_pct`: percent of pitches outside the zone that the batter swung at (Savant's `oz_swing_percent`)
  - `whiff_pct`: percent of swings that missed
  - `iso`: isolated power, slugging percentage minus batting average
  - `barrel_pct`: barrels per batted ball event, as a percent
  - `hard_hit_pct`: percent of batted balls hit 95 mph or harder
  - `sprint_speed`: feet per second in the player's fastest one-second window on competitive runs
  - `sb`: stolen bases
  - `oaa`: Outs Above Average, as a center fielder
  - `arm_mph`: average speed of the player's hardest throws from center field
- `collect.py`: the script that made `center-fielders.csv`. It downloads three Savant leaderboards as CSV and joins them on `player_id`. Rerun it with `python3 -I collect.py`.

## Who is in the table

Savant's Outs Above Average leaderboard for center fielders (`pos=8`) with its default "qualified" minimum. Every one of them also appears on the batting leaderboard (100+ plate appearances) and the arm-strength leaderboard (50+ throws), so none were dropped.

## Caveats

- `sb`, `oaa` and `hr` are counts, so they grow with playing time; the other columns are rates. Pete Crow-Armstrong had the most plate appearances (726) of the 40.
- Arm strength comes only from throws made while playing center field. The batting stats include games at other positions and as a designated hitter.
- Savant updates its stats after the fact (scoring changes, model updates), so a rerun may not match this file exactly.
